items: Copy and Paste: Transfer the entire job posting text into a separate document so you can annotate and analyze every section without losing context or formatting.
Highlight Hard Requirements: Identify every non-negotiable criterion like degrees, certifications, years of experience, and specific tools by searching for must-have language.
Identify Soft Preferences: Find skills framed as beneficial but not mandatory by looking for words like preferred, ideal, or bonus in the job posting.
Examine LinkedIn Profiles: Review 3-5 profiles of people currently working in your target role at similar companies to discover industry terms not in the posting.
Build Your Master Keyword List: Compile every noun, phrase, and technical term from hard requirements, soft preferences, and industry shorthand into one searchable document.
Add Exact Phrasing to Your List: Include the precise language used in the job posting because ATS systems match exact text rather than conceptual equivalents.
Map Accomplishments to Numbers: Replace vague descriptions like led a team with specific data points including team size, percentage improvements, and timeframes for ATS parsing.
Verify Every Keyword Appears: Cross-reference your master list against your resume to confirm each term shows up somewhere in your work history or skills section.
Quantify Impact Statements: Turn general claims into machine-readable data by including before-and-after metrics, dollar amounts, or percentage improvements for every accomplishment.
Align Vocabulary Exactly: Mirror the phrasing from job requirements verbatim on your resume so ATS systems recognize your qualifications without needing interpretation.
Check Structural Formatting: Remove tables, graphics, columns, headers, or footers that ATS systems cannot parse correctly and may cause your content to be skipped entirely.
Test Format Compatibility: Save your resume as a plain text document to verify all keywords and formatting survived the conversion before submitting online.
